indicators.note: something that drinks takes liquid in, so the word for chose swallows the litres

parts.note: chose means picked

explanation.surface: A drinker who opted to down several litres has ended up the worse for wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal slang for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Make believe there's agreement about poem

indicators.note: the agreement word goes around the poem word, enclosing it

parts.note: a pact is a formal agreement
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad

explanation.surface: A pretend world is built on a shared understanding concerning some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To playact is to pretend or perform a role, which is exactly what make-believe involves.

indicators.note: the star sign wraps around the drug's letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac
H is slang shorthand for heroin

explanation.surface: A schemer comes across a notice concerning a hard drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is someone who takes risks to exploit any opening, an opportunist.

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second, so the queue word climbs onto the river letter

parts.note: a queue is a line of people

explanation.surface: People in a queue clamber aboard a riverboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of boat on a regular route.

clue.text: Diminished worth of pamphlet during performance

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits within it, so the pamphlet goes inside the performance word

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: A leaflet handed out in the middle of a show lowered its value.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to lessen its value or take away from its merit.

clue.text: Help in making out with good girls

parts.note: lasses are girls, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: It sounds like romantic assistance from some well-behaved young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making out' suggests kissing, but here it means discerning things by sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles aid vision, helping the wearer to see or discern things clearly.

definitions.meaning: to get along well with someone, form a friendly relationship
to climb aboard a bus, train or similar vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the same phrasal verb: people who are friendly get along, and passengers climb aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to be on friendly terms and to embark on a vehicle.

parts.note: the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is its long side, the one opposite the right angle

explanation.surface: A geometry question asks whether the triangle's slanting edge is next to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a hypotenuse is literally a long side.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means next to or beside, so it describes something bordering another thing.

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready by reworking it, so the letters of the clue word are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A permit has been drawn up to assist someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but is the old noun for quietness, as in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as a noun means quiet or saying nothing, a synonym for absence of speech.

parts.note: to shy is to throw or fling, as at a coconut shy
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: Someone flings a cloak away out of nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyness is bashfulness or reticence, a close synonym of timidity.

clue.text: A Tory leader pockets profits? That's touching!

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the two outer pieces enclose the profits
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here the start of Tory

parts.note: profits are gains

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician helping himself to the money is a moving sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's touching!' reads as an emotional exclamation; it really means in physical contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning against a wall means pressing up to it, so the preposition means in contact with.

clue.text: Dolly left the French in Ilium

indicators.note: the two short pieces are placed inside the name of the ancient city

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy
le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: A doll called Dolly has been abandoned by the French in ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly' looks like a name; it is a wheeled platform used to move cameras or loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolly is a small wheeled cart or platform, a kind of trolley.

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
certain means definite or sure

explanation.surface: An instruction to verify something once it is confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain something is to find it out for sure, to verify it.

clue.text: Spiritual benefactor that is after information

indicators.note: the that-is abbreviation follows the information word in the answer

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A generous patron of the soul turns up once the facts are in.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit from Arabian tales who grants wishes, a supernatural giver of favours.

indicators.note: the church letters come further along, after the hill word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A glow can be seen from a church on the far side of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp or a burning brand carried to give light.

parts.note: the crew of a ship are its hands
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Sailors offer fish as a welcome gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking palms is a customary friendly gesture when people meet.

indicators.note: the sailors word holds the banquets word inside it

parts.note: tars is an old word for sailors
to dine is to feast, so dines means banquets as a verb

explanation.surface: Seamen running late because they are busy hosting feasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banquets' reads as a noun but is taken as the verb meaning feasts, giving DINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness means slowness to arrive or being behind time, a synonym of being late.

clue.text: One replying to research on study

parts.note: res is a common abbreviation for research
to ponder is to study or consider carefully

explanation.surface: Someone answers a questionnaire about academic investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is one who answers or reacts, so a person giving a reply.

clue.text: Steak done differently in French city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put within the name of the city

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

indicators.note: done differently means the letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A beef dish cooked another way in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a small round cut of beef fillet, a kind of steak.

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A collapse at a clay quarry is the usual sort of catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic can mean a perfect example of its kind, as in a classic mistake, which is representative.

clue.text: Religious rite gets agreement out of court

indicators.note: the agreement word lies outside the court letters, wrapping them

parts.note: a union is an agreement or alliance

explanation.surface: A church ceremony results in a settlement reached without going to trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of court' looks like the legal phrase; here it means the agreement sits outside the court letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is anointing with oil, a sacramental ceremony in the Christian church.

indicators.note: without means the resistance letter is left out of the experience word

parts.note: to endure is to experience or undergo
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Advice to put money into practical knowledge while meeting no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' suggests finance, but it means endow or furnish with a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to endow or invest them with it.

parts.note: to drop something is to give it up
sin is wrongdoing or immorality

explanation.surface: Appeals to abandon wicked ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drops in pays a casual, unannounced visit, that is, calls on a friend.

indicators.note: the conservationists' letters go within the rearranged letters
organisation means arranging the letters into a new structure

parts.note: the National Trust is a British heritage conservation charity, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: Permitting environmentalists into an exclusive society.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a right, that is, to permit or authorise them.

clue.text: Having second thoughts about one making strides

indicators.note: the second-thoughts letters go around the word for one

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone reconsidering as they walk forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second thoughts' are a PS, written after the main letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paces are steps or strides, the units of a walker's movement.

parts.note: a crow is a winged creature, so a winger's means the crow's
a foot is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: A football winger keeps a set distance from the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; it is a bird. The line is a wrinkle, not a pitch marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's foot is one of the fine wrinkles at the outer corner of the eye.

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the Tory party
a lout is a boor or yob

explanation.surface: A political oaf has sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for power or sway, especially political weight.

clue.text: Warrant officer admits fighting in a crowd

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the officer letters take the fighting word inside

parts.note: a sergeant major, SM, is a warrant officer in the British Army
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A soldier confesses to brawling amid a throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits' reads as confesses but signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large dense mass of people or insects, a throng.

clue.text: A city fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past, as in years ago

explanation.surface: An urban place that used to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major city in Illinois, USA, an example of a city.

parts.note: dead can mean exhausted, as in dead on one's feet
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A last push comes from a worn-out team.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a dead set at something is to make a resolute attempt at it, a firm push.

clue.text: Nine crashed into obstacle that's forgiving

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed into the obstacle word

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

indicators.note: something that has crashed is wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nine vehicles hit a barrier, and the authorities show mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful or tolerant, ready to pardon.

parts.note: a Roman is someone from Rome, an Italian
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A new Italian place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is a noun, a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a novel or story, typically of love or adventure.
